Let \(D\) be the top vertex, \(B\) and \(C\) the left and right base vertices, and let \(M,N\) be the marked midpoints of \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{AC}\), respectively.

The shaded plane is \(\triangle DMN\), so the part containing \(A\) is tetrahedron \(DAMN\).

Because \(M\) and \(N\) are midpoints,
\[
\frac{AM}{AB}=\frac{AN}{AC}=\frac12.
\]
Thus, using the shared angle at \(A\),
\[
\frac{[AMN]}{[ABC]}
=\frac{AM\cdot AN}{AB\cdot AC}
=\frac12\cdot\frac12
=\frac14.
\]

Tetrahedra \(DAMN\) and \(DABC\) have bases in the same plane and the same altitude from \(D\), so their volumes have the same ratio as their base areas. Therefore,
\[
V_{DAMN}=\frac14(120)=30.
\]

\[
\boxed{30}
\]
